The analyst filtered df_clean (removed QA orders) then filtered for new & paid_search. They computed fraction = n_converted / n_total. They removed QA orders (which are not new paid_search? They also didn't filter out refunded orders, but they claim converted column already 1 only for completed checkouts. Documentation says converted is 1 if order completed checkout. So refunded orders have converted maybe 0? Could be refunded orders still have converted=1? Not sure. But they rely on doc. The estimand only cares about conversion, not revenue. So okay.

Thus scope is correct.

They didn't address potential imbalance of segment/channel (non-randomized). But the estimand is descriptive, not causal, so not a problem. They also didn't address that channel is not randomized, but not needed. So no unacknowledged problem.

5. FALSE PREMISE: Premises verified: they printed that new and paid_search exist. So fine.
